successors.name: Majapahit
successors.text: the Sumatran land of the Srivijaya shape of 1293 that Cliopatria's Majapahit shape of 1294 covers

successors.name: Malaya (Malay Peninsula principalities)
successors.text: the Malay Peninsula land of the Srivijaya shape of 1293 that Cliopatria's Malaya shape of 1294 covers

ledger.x: c. 682-685: Srivijaya conquers Kedah. Infobox 'Conquest of Kedah: c. 682-685'. Cliopatria draws Kedah only from 692, and the Chola page (1025) shows the Srivijaya fleet based at Kedah.
686: the Kota Kapur stone is carved after a conquest.

c. 718: Srivijaya reaches the Isthmus of Kra (Cliopatria's year; the page is silent on 718). 'Langkasuka on the Malay Peninsula became part of Srivijaya' (7th century); Maharaja Dharmasetu 'ordered the construction of three sanctuaries' at Ligor (c. 775).
1026: the raids end with the king in Chola hands.
1139: Kedah leaves Srivijaya (Cliopatria's year; the pages opened are silent on 1139).
1139: the peninsula north of Kedah leaves Srivijaya (Cliopatria's year; page silent).

c. 1202: Jambi leaves Srivijaya's orbit. 'Jambi became independent from Sanfoqi's influence in the early 13th century'; the year is the Cliopatria row boundary within that span. The Melayu page has Jambi leading the Sanfoqi missions from the 11th century and Malayu embassies to China in 1299 and 1301.
1293: Cliopatria's Srivijaya ends, the year the Majapahit is founded.

wars.name: Srivijayan campaign against Java
wars.outcome: Outcome unrecorded: the inscription is carved as 'the Srivijaya army just departed to attack Java'.

wars.name: Conquest of Kedah
wars.outcome: Kedah becomes Srivijayan (infobox 'Conquest of Kedah: c.

wars.name: Mataram-Srivijayan wars
wars.outcome: No land changes hands: the Anjukladang inscription of 937, Dharmawangsa's naval invasion of 990 and Srivijaya's repulse of the Javanese in 1006; the infobox gives 'c.

wars.name: Chola invasion of Srivijaya
wars.outcome: Chola victory: King Sangrama Vijayottunggavarman captured, Palembang ransacked, the Srivijayan maritime monopoly broken.

wars.name: Pamalayu expedition
wars.outcome: Singhasari sends the expedition in 1275 (decreed) to Melayu; the Melayu page has Palembang and Jambi taken in 1288; the force returns to Java on 3 May 1293.

certainty.note: A mandala of ports and river mouths; the pages give no frontier.
